The update comes from approximating the score function near $\esttmp{\param}$
by its first-order
[Taylor polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor%27s_theorem):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\score(\param)
&\approx \score^*(\param)\\
&\eqdef \score(\esttmp{\param}) + \hess(\esttmp{\param})(\param - \esttmp{\param})
\end{aligned}
$$

The approximate score function $\score^*(\param)$ is linear in $\param$,
so the approximate score equation $\score^*(\param) = 0$
is easy to solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= \score(\esttmp{\param}) + \hess(\esttmp{\param})(\param - \esttmp{\param})
&& \text{(set $\score^*(\param) = 0$)}\\
-\score(\esttmp{\param}) &= \hess(\esttmp{\param})(\param - \esttmp{\param})
&& \text{(subtract $\score(\esttmp{\param})$)}\\
-\inv{\hess(\esttmp{\param})}\score(\esttmp{\param}) &= \param - \esttmp{\param}
&& \text{(multiply by $\inv{\hess(\esttmp{\param})}$ on the left)}\\
\param &= \esttmp{\param} - \inv{\hess(\esttmp{\param})}\score(\esttmp{\param})
&& \text{(add $\esttmp{\param}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

and the solution becomes the next guess.
